question: What happens if useEffect has no dependency array?

choices.text: The effect runs only once on mount
The effect runs after every re-render

explanation: Without a dependency array, useEffect runs after every render. Use [] for mount-only, or [dep] to re-run when dep changes.

wrong_explanations.a: That is the behavior of useEffect with an empty dependency array [].
wrong_explanations.c: useEffect always runs at least once after render.
wrong_explanations.d: It does not throw — this is React's default behavior.

best_practices: Always specify the dependency array explicitly
Avoid infinite loops: do not set state in an effect without conditions
Use eslint-plugin-react-hooks to catch missing deps
learning_objective: Understand useEffect lifecycle and dependency arrays

question: Which is the correct way to declare state in React?

choices.text: let count = 0 inside a function component

explanation: useState returns a [value, setter] tuple and triggers a re-render when the setter is called.

wrong_explanations.b: A plain let variable does not trigger re-renders.
wrong_explanations.c: this.state is for class components, not modern function components.
wrong_explanations.d: useRef is for values that should not trigger re-renders; interactive UI state uses useState.

best_practices: Use useState for state that affects the UI
Do not mutate state directly — use the setter
Group related state or consider useReducer for complex logic

question: What is the purpose of key on a React list?

choices.text: Help React identify items that changed, were added, or removed
Required for CSS grid to work

explanation: Stable keys help the reconciler preserve the correct item state when a list is reordered or filtered.

wrong_explanations.c: CSS grid does not depend on React keys.
wrong_explanations.d: React keys are internal and differ from DOM id attributes.

best_practices: Use stable ids from data, not array index when order can change
Keys must be unique among siblings
Do not generate random keys on every render

question: In CSS Flexbox, which property controls spacing along the main axis?
explanation: justify-content distributes space on the main axis; align-items on the cross axis.

wrong_explanations.a: align-items aligns on the cross axis, not the main axis.
wrong_explanations.c: flex-wrap controls whether items wrap to a new line.
wrong_explanations.d: gap helps spacing but justify-content distributes along the main axis.

best_practices: Learn the difference between main axis and cross axis
Use gap for consistent spacing between items
Combine justify-content and align-items to center content

question: What is the output of typeof null in JavaScript?
explanation: typeof null === "object" is a historical JS quirk kept for compatibility.

wrong_explanations.a: There is no typeof primitive named "null".
wrong_explanations.c: undefined is only for unassigned variables.

best_practices: Use === null for explicit null checks
Use Array.isArray to check arrays
Understand null vs undefined in API design
learning_objective: Understand typeof and null in JavaScript

question: When should event handlers be defined inline in JSX?

choices.text: Avoid if it creates a new function every render without need

explanation: Inline arrows in JSX create a new function each render; for memoized children, extract with useCallback.

wrong_explanations.a: Inline is fine for simple handlers, but not always best practice.
wrong_explanations.c: Inline handlers are valid and common for simple cases.
wrong_explanations.d: Function components use JSX handlers too.

best_practices: useCallback for handlers passed to memoized components
Extract complex handlers to named functions
Do not prematurely optimize cheap handlers

question: What is the role of semantic HTML like <main> and <nav>?

choices.text: SEO only, no effect on accessibility
Help assistive technology understand page structure

explanation: Landmark elements provide meaningful navigation for screen readers and keyboard users.

wrong_explanations.a: Semantic HTML also matters for accessibility, not just SEO.
wrong_explanations.c: div is still valid for layout without semantic meaning.
wrong_explanations.d: CSS does not require semantic tags.

best_practices: One <main> per page
Use a logical h1–h6 heading hierarchy
Label forms with <label htmlFor>

question: What is a controlled component?

choices.text: An input whose value is driven by React state
A component only editable by admins

explanation: Controlled input: value + onChange connected to React state — single source of truth.

wrong_explanations.c: PropTypes/TypeScript are separate from controlled vs uncontrolled.
wrong_explanations.d: Context does not define controlled components.

best_practices: Single source of truth for form values
Validate before submit
Consider react-hook-form for large forms
